overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's account of habit and incorporation. You'll be asked about habit as motor knowledge, the typist, the organist, the blind person's cane, and incorporation vs. rule-following.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A skilled typist can't say where the letter "q" is without moving her fingers. What does Merleau-Ponty conclude?

options.html: That her typing depends on memorized rules she's forgotten
options.text: That her typing depends on memorized rules she's forgotten
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty's point is that her knowledge was never a stored rule. It's available only in typing.

options.html: That her knowledge of the keyboard exists only in typing
options.text: That her knowledge of the keyboard exists only in typing
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The keyboard has become part of her bodily space. The knowledge is motor, not statable.

options.html: That typing is a mechanical reflex, needing no knowledge
options.text: That typing is a mechanical reflex, needing no knowledge
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Typing is flexible, which a reflex account can't explain. The knowledge exists in the typing itself.

options.html: That she has a mental map of the keyboard she can't access
options.text: That she has a mental map of the keyboard she can't access
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty denies there's a map. The knowledge exists only in typing.

forms.stemHtml: How does the organist prepare to play an unfamiliar organ in about an hour?

options.html: By memorizing the position of each stop and pedal
options.text: By memorizing the position of each stop and pedal
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. He couldn't recite the positions afterward. He settles into the instrument's space.

options.html: By settling into the instrument's expressive space
options.text: By settling into the instrument's expressive space
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! He takes up the organ's dimensions and directions as one settles into a house.

options.html: By calculating the distances between keyboards
options.text: By calculating the distances between keyboards
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty denies that the organist measures or calculates. He inhabits the instrument's space.

options.html: By practicing each piece until it becomes a reflex
options.text: By practicing each piece until it becomes a reflex
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. An hour isn't enough for new reflexes. The organist settles into the instrument's expressive space.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following fit Merleau-Ponty's account of the blind person's cane? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The cane's tip becomes an area of sensitivity
options.text: The cane's tip becomes an area of sensitivity
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! For the experienced user, sensation is felt at the tip.

options.html: The cane is no longer perceived for itself
options.text: The cane is no longer perceived for itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The user perceives through the cane, not the cane.

options.html: The cane's reach is felt as the reach of touch
options.text: The cane's reach is felt as the reach of touch
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The user doesn't calculate its length. Its reach is felt directly.

options.html: The user feels mainly pressure in the palm
options.text: The user feels mainly pressure in the palm
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's how a new user feels the cane. The experienced user feels the world at its tip.

options.html: The user calculates the cane's length each step
options.text: The user calculates the cane's length each step
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The cane's length isn't calculated. Its reach is felt directly.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for the process by which a tool becomes part of the body schema, so that one perceives and acts through it rather than perceiving it as an object? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An incorporated tool is lived through, not perceived as an object.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Extension is the resulting enlargement of the body's reach. The process is incorporation.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The process is called incorporation.

forms.stemHtml: How does incorporation differ from intellectual rule-following as an account of skill?

options.html: Incorporation is slower but more accurate than rule-following
options.text: Incorporation is slower but more accurate than rule-following
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The difference isn't speed. In incorporation, the tool is part of the lived body, and new situations are met directly.

options.html: In incorporation, the tool is part of the lived body
options.text: In incorporation, the tool is part of the lived body
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Rule-following treats the tool as an object represented in thought. Incorporation takes it into the body schema.

options.html: Incorporation applies only to tools, rule-following to skills
options.text: Incorporation applies only to tools, rule-following to skills
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both are accounts of skilled tool use. They differ over whether the tool is part of the lived body.

options.html: Incorporation requires stating the rules out loud
options.text: Incorporation requires stating the rules out loud
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Incorporated skill typically can't be stated as rules at all.

title: Habit and Incorporation
